dhp320:1: Even as an elephant engaged in the fray withstands arrows shot from the bow,
dhp320:3: So also must I bear abuse, for the multitude is wicked.
dhp321:1: It is a tamed elephant they lead to battle; it is a tamed elephant the king mounts;
dhp321:3: It is the tamed that is best among men, he that endures abuse patiently.
dhp322:1: Of surpassing excellence are mules which are tamed, and well-bred Sindh horses,
dhp322:3: And great elephants of the jungle; but better yet is the man who has tamed himself.
dhp323:1: For it is not on riding-animals such as these that one may go to that region to which one has not yet gone;
dhp323:3: Tamed must one go upon the tamed; namely, upon one’s own well-tamed self.
dhp324:1: The elephant Dhanapāla, with pungent juice flowing from his temples, hard to restrain,
dhp324:3: Eats not a morsel so long as he is held captive; the elephant remembers the elephant-grove.
dhp325:1: If a man gives way to indolence, eats overmuch,
dhp325:2: Spends his time in sleep, and lies and rolls about
dhp325:3: Like a great hog fed on grain,
dhp325:4: Such a simpleton will enter the womb again and again.
dhp326:1: These thoughts of mine once wandered hither and thither
dhp326:2: Wherever they liked, wherever they desired, wherever they pleased;
dhp326:3: But hereafter I shall control them perfectly,
dhp326:4: Even as an elephant-driver controls an elephant in rut with his hook.
dhp327:1: Be joyful in heedfulness, guard well your thoughts.
dhp327:3: Extricate yourselves from the quagmire, even as an elephant that is stuck fast in the mud.
dhp328:1: Should one find a prudent companion to walk with, an upright man and steadfast,
dhp328:3: Let one walk with him, joyful, mindful, overcoming all dangers.
dhp329:1: Should one not find a prudent companion to walk with, an upright man and steadfast,
dhp329:2: Then, like a king renouncing the kingdom he has conquered, let one walk alone,
dhp329:3: Like an elephant roaming at will in an elephant-forest.
dhp330:1: The life of solitude is better; one cannot be friends with a simpleton;
dhp330:3: Free from desire, like an elephant roaming at will in an elephant-forest.
dhp331:1: When need arises, pleasant are companions;
dhp331:2: Pleasant is enjoyment, when one shares it with another;
dhp331:3: Works of merit give pleasure at the hour of death;
dhp331:4: Pleasant is it to leave behind all suffering.
dhp332:1: Pleasant is motherhood in this world, and pleasant is fatherhood;
dhp332:3: Pleasant is the estate of a monk in this world, and pleasant is the estate of a Brahman.
dhp333:1: Pleasant is a life of righteousness unto old age, pleasant is faith firmly established,
dhp333:3: Pleasant is the attainment of wisdom, pleasant is the avoiding of evil.
